data.title: CrowdStrike jumps 14% amid cybersecurity sector rally
data.description:
Shares of CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD), a cloud-native cybersecurity company behind the AI-centered Falcon platform, soared just over 14% on Monday. The stock closed at $235.49, a gain of $28.75 on the session, amid renewed investor focus on cybersecurity as a beneficiary of growing artificial intelligence risks. 

Cybersecurity stocks broadly advanced as investors rotated into the sector on the view that securing AI systems, enterprise identities, and cloud workloads represents a durable growth opportunity. Evercore ISI analyst Kirk Materne was cited as arguing that demand for cybersecurity should hold up regardless of the pace of frontier AI model development. data.title: 3 things to look out for on Tuesday
data.description:
Wall Street finished lower on Monday as investors weighed developments in the artificial intelligence space and monitored oil prices after a sharp rally.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended -0.2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) handed back -0.5%.

Now, here are three things to look out for on Tuesday:

  • The Federal Reserve Bank of New York will release its September reading on the NY Empire State Manufacturing Index, which is expected to weaken to 14.10 from 20.60 in the prior month.
  • Corteva (CTVA) will hold an investor day event to discuss the separation of its advanced seed and genetics business into a standalone, publicly traded company called Vylor.
  • Marvel's Wolverine videogame will be released. Disney-owned (DIS) Marvel is releasing the game exclusively on Sony's (SONY) PlayStation 5.

data.title: Abbott Laboratories jumps after six straight sessions of losses
data.description:
Abbott Laboratories (ABT) snapped six consecutive sessions of losses as the stock gained 1.21% to close at $103.18 on Monday.

Shares of the global healthcare giant were largely flat in early trading but rose after announcing that it has  agreed to pay the Department of Justice $385M to resolve claims related to its 2022 recall of baby formula manufactured at a Michigan plant in which deadly bacteria allegedly killed two infants.

The company has admitted no wrongdoing, and the settlement does not represent an admission of guilt, it said.

The drugmaker lost over 6% in the previous six sessions. On a YTD basis, Abbott has declined nearly 18%, while in the past year it has seen a fall of 21% compared to a 16% rise in the broader markets.

On September 8, Abbott announced the FDA approval of its TactiFlex Duo ablation catheter, designed to treat complex cases of atrial fibrillation with a combination of pulsed-field ablation technology and radiofrequency energy. However, the stock ended 2.59% lower at $105.52.

Looking at Seeking Alpha’s quant rating, the stock has a Hold rating with a score of 3.25 out of 5. ABT has been rated an A+ for profitability but is dragged down by a D grade for valuation. 

However, Seeking Alpha and Wall Street analysts share a consensus rating of Buy.

In August, the pharma firm was  downgraded by Seeking Alpha analyst Gen Alpha to Buy from Strong Buy over its high valuation. However, it remained optimistic over the firm’s renewed momentum across nutrition, diagnostics, and medical devices.

“Abbott Laboratories remains a compelling long-term investment despite trading near its historical valuation. Its diversified healthcare portfolio is showing renewed momentum. This has been supported by recovery in Nutrition and continued medical-device innovation,” the analyst said.

data.title: Starbucks snaps six straight sessions of losses
data.description:
Starbucks (SBUX) shares snapped six straight sessions of losses, as the stock closed 0.4% higher at $99.12 on Monday.

The coffee giant lost about 7% in the preceding six sessions. Overall, the stock has risen nearly 18% so far this year, compared to the 12% growth in the broader S&P 500 Index.

SBUX is down nearly 8% over the past one month. The stock closed 0.5% lower on Friday at $98.74.

Recently, the company was in focus after facing activist pressure once again as SOC Investment Group filed a shareholder proposal with the SEC last week looking to separate the CEO and board chair roles at the company.

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, SBUX has a Hold rating with a score of 3.38 out of 5. The company received an A in the prospect of profitability, while it got an F in the valuation factor.

Turning to the Wall Street community, 16 analysts gave SBUX a Buy and above, 17 analysts have given the stock a Hold recommendation, and three recommended Sell or lower. Seeking Alpha analysts are also cautious and see the stock as a Hold.

“The company is doing a lot of things right at the moment. But this does not necessarily mean that investors should take a bullish stance on the company from an investment standpoint. The firm has a lot going for it right now. But as it’s priced, I think that it justifies nothing better than a ‘hold’ rating,” said Seeking Alpha analyst Daniel Jones.

Another Seeking Alpha analyst, IWA Research, noted that Starbucks is a Hold, as the “valuation remains fair and already seems to take into account its turnaround potential, making the risk-reward unattractive to justify buying now.”

data.title: SA analyst warns market complacency could give way to sharp volatility
data.description:
Wall Street slipped Monday as investors assessed renewed Middle East tensions, rising oil prices, and uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence spending ahead of the Federal Reserve’s pivotal meeting this week.

Seeking Alpha analyst Damir Tokic warned that markets remain overly calm despite several developments that could trigger larger price swings. 

“Markets remain complacent,” Tokic stated, pointing to a brief move in the 10-year Treasury yield above 5% before rates retreated, as well as a sharp oil-price spike that subsequently moderated. 

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) fell -0.2%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) declined -0.3% and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) dropped -0.4%. 

Tokic argued that the market’s muted response is occurring even as geopolitical risks intensify and questions surrounding the sustainability of the AI boom continue to grow. 

He also highlighted uncertainty surrounding the Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy decision, adding another potential source of volatility for investors.

“In my opinion, volatility is likely to sharply rise, and stay high leading into the midterms,” Tokic said. 

The analyst’s warning comes as investors balance competing forces, including elevated Treasury yields, higher energy prices, and concerns about AI investment, against continued strength in equities. 

With Middle East tensions escalating and the U.S. midterm elections approaching, Tokic expects financial markets could face a more volatile environment in the months ahead.

data.title: Bank of America plunges on CEO's sales, trading revenue guidance; bank stocks sell off
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) was trading lower after CEO Brian Moynihan said the lender's quarterly sales and trading revenue would be "flat" year-over-year.

Shares were down 5.29% to $59.38 before the market closed on Monday.

"It'll be one of the better third quarters we've ever had-but it'll be relatively flat to last year, because last year was a big recovery from the second quarter," said the CEO at Barclays' 24th Annual Global Financial Services Conference.

Furthermore, he expects investment banking fees to decline by ~10% from the prior year to ~$1.6B-$1.8B.

Meanwhile, net interest income is projected to be at the upper end of the 6%-8% range for 2026.

Bank stocks sold off on the news. Invesco KBW Bank ETF (KBWB) was down 1.95% to $94.96.

Goldman Sachs (GS) fell 3.99% to $988.15; Morgan Stanley (MS) 3.41% to $207.06; Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) 3.13% to $157.57; Wells Fargo (WFC) 1.96% to $88.52; JPMorgan Chase (JPM) 1.68% to $350.25; Citigroup (C) 0.85% to $137.64; and U.S. Bancorp (USB) 0.37% to $62.61.
